Spring simple rules for leash checks for new staff
This page helps new colleagues see a habit of care

This page sets the standard for our Companion Animal Travel Desk at Aurelia Skyways. It matters because every animal file reflects a promise to the traveler, to the cabin team, and to the ground staff who handle each journey with steady attention. New staff should treat each case as routine work that still deserves careful eyes, calm language, and prompt follow-through.

Begin each contact with a warm professional tone. Ask for the travel details that belong in the record, confirm the animal's condition, and listen for concerns about crate fit, feeding, medication, or stress. Keep the exchange orderly. If a traveler seems uncertain, guide the conversation in clear steps and avoid hurried phrasing. A simple and respectful manner helps people trust the desk and helps you gather accurate information.

Check that the documents in front of you are complete and readable. Verify the animal's identity, the travel route, and any handling notes that affect acceptance or transfer. When the record is incomplete, pause the process and request the missing item before moving ahead. Never guess at a detail. The desk depends on accuracy more than speed.

Coordinate with the cabin team when the booking calls for live oversight during flight. Their monitoring report is part of the full service chain, and your notes must support it without confusion. Use plain language in the file so the crew can act quickly if the animal needs quiet, water, or separation from noise. If a traveler mentions a pet such as Baxter, record the name exactly as provided and keep the tone steady and reassuring.

Maintain courtesy throughout the day, even during busy periods. The desk is a point of contact, not a place for debate. If a request falls outside policy, state the limit cleanly and direct the traveler to the next suitable option. Good operations rely on consistent handling, clear handoffs, and disciplined follow-up from the first call to the final confirmation.

Remember to stay calm, precise, and courteous in every animal case.
